note: Forge-native unit names (metre, kilometre, inch, nautical-mile, astronomical-unit, light-year, and so on) instead of CyberChef's menu, with a source and a target unit. The sum is exact: every unit is an exact ratio of the metre (international yard and pound of 1959, NIST SP 811), the value is decimal text with an optional sign and exponent, and the result is rounded half away from zero to a number of significant digits (20 by default) and written in plain decimal form. No parsec (it is not a rational number of metres). A value that is not a number is E_COERCE.
Same design as Convert distance: exact ratios of the square metre (the acre is 4046.8564224 m2), Forge-native unit names, significant digits for the rounding.

Same design as Convert distance: exact ratios of the kilogram (the international pound is 0.45359237 kg; the grain, carat and troy ounce are exact), Forge-native unit names, significant digits for the rounding.
Same design as Convert distance: exact ratios of the metre per second (the knot is 1852 m per hour, the mile per hour 0.44704 m/s). Mach is not offered, because it depends on the air.

Same design as Convert distance: bits, nibbles, bytes, the decimal units (kilo to exa, powers of 1000) and the binary units (kibi to exbi, IEC 80000-13, powers of 1024), as bits and as bytes. Exact; the rounding is to significant digits.

One op with a source format (auto detects it), a target format and a precision. Formats: decimal degrees, degrees and decimal minutes, degrees minutes and seconds, geohash, UTM and MGRS (WGS 84, 80 S to 84 N; Karney's series, sub-millimetre). Degrees convert exactly (whole numbers of 10^-12 degree). The Ordnance Survey National Grid is not offered: it needs the OSGB36 datum shift, which cannot be done exactly from a published formula. CyberChef's delimiter and direction menus are replaced by a reader that accepts any separator and the letters N S E W before or after the numbers; the output always writes the hemisphere letters (degrees notations) or a sign (decimal degrees). MGRS and geohash input is read as the middle of its cell.

The two positions are on two lines, each in any format that Convert co-ordinate format reads; the radius is a number in kilometres (6371 by default); the result is in metres to the millimetre, as decimal text.

file-mode:parse reads an octal mode (755, 4755) or symbolic text (rwxr-xr-x, with the ls -l file type character if you like) and writes the octal and symbolic forms, the type, a table of read, write and execute for user, group and other, and the set-user-ID, set-group-ID and sticky bits, as plain text. file-mode:convert only changes the notation (octal or symbolic).
The first 8 hex digits of the 24-digit ObjectID as seconds since the epoch, written as an ISO 8601 UTC time with a .000 fraction.

Reads hex (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits, with or without #), rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla() and cmyk() and writes a text report of hex, RGB, RGBA, HSL, HSLA and CMYK with whole-number channels; CyberChef also draws a colour swatch, and Forge's ops return text. Colour names are not read.
